items.title: Johnny St. Cyr Interview, 1958-08-27
items.q: Because I was asking for instance, Ed Garland, in playing his bass

ctx.x: No, no, that was in the mind. Yes, yeah. A little mind.

Because I was asking for instance, Ed Garland, in playing his bass, in which he doesn't have the same problem quite as you playing the chords. No. But they do play chords on the bass too, you know. Oh yes. And I asked him if he was conscious of the chords as he played them and he said no, hardly ever. He said I could be talking to somebody. And he'd be playing his bass and yet his fingers would find the right chords on any piece that he knew. He never, as he knew a piece, he never thought of what chord he or even…
Well, I, there's lots of guys can do that.

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1971-04-20
items.q: I thought, didn't Johnny St. Cyr used to work for Frank Early if I remember right?

ctx.x: I thought, didn't Johnny St. Cyr used to work for Frank Early if I remember right?
Alright, we can turn it off. Tell me about, did you ever know Buddy Bolden? Did you ever hear him?

items.title: 68090_Ed Garland oral history interview
items.q: But Johnny St. Cyr was playing banjo-guitar.

ctx.x: So, then, when Johnny St. Cyr plays the banjo with the Hot Five recordings, about 1924, with Louis Armstrong, then what was that about?
Oh, well, banjos was played. They was all playing banjos after that. But Johnny St. Cyr was playing banjo-guitar.
